falsifier: Three independent falsifiers, one per cut. (1) THE B/V CUT: any shape-B member (destination callee-saved) whose surplus copy is removed by a source edit -- declaration order or otherwise -- falsifies the clause-(a) half and reopens 40 functions; run `python tools/gdl/composed_census/al_dest_split.py` for the current membership and probe any row it prints under B. (2) THE POLARITY CUT, which is the load-bearing and least-tested claim here: it rests on TWO probes, one each way, so it is the weakest link by construction. ProcessCritterList is the one untried row carrying the responsive polarity -- if a declaration-order swap there is NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, the polarity stops predicting and the reachable remainder is ZERO, not one. Conversely if either check_prefs_loaded or setup_vmu_entries (both mirror polarity) DOES respond to a declaration-order swap, the polarity cut is wrong in the other direction and all three mirror rows come back onto the queue. (3) THE ATTRIBUTION: the split is falsified if al_dest_split's shape or polarity disagrees with the aligned `fnasm <unit> <fn> --diff` view on any row -- the tool reads the copy's destination out of our own object and classifies it against CS = r14..r31, and reads polarity from whether the @lo addi's dst equals its src, so a row where the surplus copy is not the instruction it paired is a mis-attribution.

value: THE 'ADDR16_LO HOME COPY CLASS' IS NOT ONE CLASS, AND ITS REACHABLE REMAINDER IS ONE FUNCTION. Every roster of it published so far counts two shapes together, and the two have OPPOSITE dispositions, so the combined roster is unworkable as a work queue and its size has been overstating the opportunity by roughly ten to one. claim.law.pointer-decl-order-flips-addrlo-inplace-vs-fresh-destination.20260901.v1 already named the discriminant -- the DESTINATION register of the paid copy -- but no census had ever applied it, and claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1's 40-function P roster is built on the union ('paid-copy count, CS *and* volatile homes'), as is the run-53 re-measurement. SPLIT IT AND THE NUMBERS ARE: shape B, destination CALLEE-SAVED (`lis rT,SYM@ha ; addi rV,rT,SYM@lo ; mr rCS,rV`), 40 functions -- clause (a), source-unreachable, S=0 image-wide, do not probe; shape V, destination VOLATILE (`... ; mr rVOL,rT`), 5 functions -- clause (b), where declaration ORDER is a live lever. MEASURED at run 53 with tools/gdl/composed_census/al_dest_split.py: of the 45-function P roster, 40 are B, 5 are V (_AdsThread, ProcessCritterList, check_prefs_loaded, setup_vmu_entries and move_logic22). ONE TU CARRIES BOTH AND IS THE CLEANEST DEMONSTRATION: in game/enemy/enemy, fn_80046680 is shape B -- target `@0x70 addi r26,r3,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)` against ours `@0x70 addi r0,r3,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)` then `@0x74 mr r26,r0`, destination r26 callee-saved -- while move_logic22 is shape V -- target `@0x164 addi r4,r3,0 @sMilestones(ADDR16_LO)` against ours `@0x164 addi r3,r3,0 @sMilestones(ADDR16_LO)` then `@0x17c mr r4,r3`, destination r4 volatile. A ONE-LINE declaration-order swap took the V member from T227/O228 to T227/O227 with an IDENTICAL multiset (attempt.AL_movelogic22-decl-order-closes-the-volatile-half-and-both-mandated-levers-are-neutral-identical.20260904.v1, commit cdf25509e); the same class of edit is vetoed on the B member by clause (a). SECOND CUT, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE QUEUE: shape V is ITSELF two sub-polarities, and only one of them is what clause (b) actually describes. Clause (b)'s text is 'our build folds the low half onto the @ha temp IN PLACE where the target writes a FRESH register'. Test that literally -- does OUR `addi` write the register that held the @ha (dst == src), and does the TARGET's write a different one -- and the five V rows split 2 / 3. RESPONSIVE POLARITY (ours-in-place / target-fresh): move_logic22 (ours `addi r3,r3,0 @sMilestones(ADDR16_LO)`, target `addi r4,r3,0 @sMilestones(ADDR16_LO)`) and ProcessCritterList. MIRROR POLARITY (ours-fresh / target-in-place, i.e. the reverse of what the law describes): _AdsThread (ours `@0x2c addi r3,r4,0 <gADS>` then the copy `@0x30 addi r4,r3,0`, against the target lowering into r4 in place with no copy at all), check_prefs_loaded and setup_vmu_entries. THE POLARITY PREDICTED BOTH PROBES RUN THIS RUN, 2 for 2: move_logic22 (responsive polarity) responded to the one-line declaration-order swap; _AdsThread (mirror polarity) was NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL under the identical class of edit -- `ADSTREAM* base = &gADS;` moved from sixth position to second, ahead of all four int locals, left our object's word digest for the function at ca738c8fc6a9 in both states (attempt.AL_adsthread-the-mirror-polarity-does-not-respond-to-declaration-order.20260904.v1). CONSEQUENCE FOR PLANNING, and it is the whole point of this law: a work order promising that closing this class yields '40+ functions' is promising the unreachable half. Of 45 P rows, 40 are clause (a), 3 are the mirror polarity that does not respond, 1 is closed, and the reachable remainder is ONE function -- ProcessCritterList, in game/enemy/critter, whose eight webfrank pins belong to another lane. There is no flip path for any TU here.
